justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are explicitly covered: Video Session Manager for consultations (R-01), E-Prescription Integrator for pharmacy dispatch (R-02), AI Symptom Checker Service for triage (R-03), and Consent & Policy Engine with WASM / Lua Consent Filter for granular data sharing consent (R-04).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Media Gateway Controller implements adaptive bitrate control for degraded modes. gRPC-Web and API Client & Sync Engine minimize payload overhead, while Session State Coordinator (Redis) and Offline Local Store provide multi-tiered caching for rapid state access.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability targets (R-08) are directly met by Enterprise Message Router supporting HL7 FHIR and national EU formats when interfacing with Regional Pharmacy Networks. Identity federation integrates smoothly with Regional Identity Providers via OAuth 2.0 / OIDC.
justifications.usability: Web & Mobile Client Apps provide UI Layer & State Manager for patients and clinicians, backed by Offline Local Store for intermittent connections. Compliance Officers have a dedicated Data Access Layer. However, specialized clinician workflows are minimally differentiated in client apps.
justifications.reliability: Fault tolerance is robustly addressed by Pharmacy Circuit Breaker Service and DLQ Error Buffer. Low-bandwidth stability is handled by Offline Local Store, Media Gateway Controller adaptive bitrate, and Session State Coordinator's 60-second reconnection grace period.
justifications.security: Residency and privacy constraints (R-05, GDPR, HIPAA) are strictly enforced by Data Sync & Residency Enforcer, Consent & Policy Engine, and VPC Service Controls. mTLS, OAuth2/PKCE, SQLCipher, and BigQuery Audit & Traceability Engine ensure end-to-end security and traceability.
justifications.maintainability: The architecture exhibits high cohesion and loose coupling across modular services (Core Telehealth Service, AI Symptom Checker Service, Video Session Manager). Responsibilities are isolated with clean internal gRPC and SPIFFE/SPIRE interfaces, facilitating independent updates and testability.
justifications.portability: The design aligns cleanly with target GCP regions (Cloud Run, BigQuery, Vertex AI, Cloud SQL). However, tight coupling to proprietary GCP managed services reduces easy replaceability or migration across non-GCP cloud providers if required.

PERF-01.justification: The WebRTC SFU Media Gateway Controller and Redis-backed session coordinator support low-latency setup, though managing 5,000 concurrent media streams on custom SFU infrastructure introduces operational scaling sensitivity.
sensitivity_points: SFU auto-scaling responsiveness under sudden peak European traffic surges
tradeoffs: Self-hosting Mediasoup SFUs gives traffic control but increases cluster orchestration complexity

PERF-02.justification: Serverless Cloud Run auto-scaling combined with Vertex AI inference and asynchronous BigQuery Storage Write API logging comfortably handles 14-50 QPS while maintaining sub-3s latencies.
sensitivity_points: Vertex AI inference latency and Cloud Run container cold start times
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit logging guarantees low latency at the risk of slight buffering lag

AVAIL-01.justification: The SFU Media Gateway Controller implements adaptive bitrate streaming, Redis coordinates a 60-second reconnection window, and the client Offline Local Store prevents any loss of clinical notes.
sensitivity_points: Threshold sensitivity when downscaling video to audio-only at sub-300 kbit/s
tradeoffs: Dropping video quality preserves audio continuity and consultation integrity

AVAIL-02.justification: The deployment target specifies only us-central1 and europe-west3. Since data residency strictly forbids failing over US data to the EU, an outage in us-central1 lacks a secondary US region to recover within 1 hour.
sensitivity_points: Absence of a defined secondary US failover region in GCP target configuration
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents cross-region disaster failover to the operational EU region

MOD-01.justification: The Enterprise Message Router within E-Prescription Integrator uses Spring Integration to decouple integration logic, isolating new national EU formats and adapters from core telehealth services.
sensitivity_points: Extensibility of payload transformation interfaces for varying EU prescription schemas
tradeoffs: Centralizing integration adapters adds routing complexity inside the integrator service

MOD-02.justification: Inference outputs are tied directly to model versions via the Audit & Traceability Component and logged into BigQuery, while Cloud Run and Vertex AI enable immediate version rollbacks.
sensitivity_points: Consistent propagation of model version metadata from Vertex AI to BigQuery audit logs
tradeoffs: Detailed per-inference lineage logging increases storage volume for explainability and compliance

SEC-01.justification: The Consent & Policy Engine (OPA) coupled with WASM filters and VPC Service Controls verifies patient consent tokens before routing queries across regional databases, logging all access in BigQuery.
sensitivity_points: Strict evaluation of regional cross-border consent policies before database querying
tradeoffs: Policy evaluation on every data fetch introduces slight processing latency for security

SEC-02.justification: Withdrawal updates the Consent & Policy Engine dynamically, immediately cutting off access. However, specific mechanisms for purging previously synchronized research datasets within BigQuery are not fully articulated.
sensitivity_points: Propagation delay of consent revocation events across asynchronous data pipelines
tradeoffs: Immediate policy enforcement stops queries instantly without waiting for batched downstream pipeline purges
